text:
Obama 
Chelsea Manning
Army intelligence analyst convicted of leaking hundreds of thousands of classified military and diplomatic documents to WikiLeaks. Obama commuted the remaining 28 years of a 35-year sentence so Manning would be released after roughly seven years. Republicans including Sen. John McCain, Rep. Mac Thornberry, and House Speaker Paul Ryan called it outrageous, and an act that treated “espionage” lightly and put troops at risk. Critics labeled Manning a traitor; supporters called the original sentence excessive. The commutation stood; 

https://t.co/q351UAZrzP

Oscar López Rivera
Member of the FALN, a Puerto Rican nationalist group that claimed responsibility for dozens of bombings in U.S. cities in the 1970s–80s. He was serving a long sentence for seditious conspiracy and related charges (not a specific bombing conviction). Obama commuted it so he would be released after 36 years. Victims’ families (including an op-ed by the son of a Fraunces Tavern bombing victim), columnists, and some law-enforcement voices condemned the decision and described López Rivera as a terrorist. Supporters called him a political prisoner. Clinton had previously offered him conditional clemency, which he declined. Again, the grant was public and was not reversed. 

https://t.co/b31RV1PJsf
High profile pardons
James Cartwright — retired Marine general, pleaded guilty to lying to the FBI in a leak probe related to Stuxnet/Iran. Pardon, not a commutation from a long sentence.
 pardons such as Willie McCovey (tax evasion) and Ian Schrager (Studio 54 tax case).
Biden
Hunter Biden (pardon, December 1, 2024)
Son of the president. Convicted on federal gun and tax charges; about to be sentenced. Biden issued a broad pardon covering offenses from January 1, 2014 through December 1, 2024 — after repeatedly saying he would not pardon him.

Leonard Peltier (commutation, last hours of the presidency)
Native American activist convicted of the 1975 murders of two FBI agents on the Pine Ridge Reservation. Life sentence commuted; he was released to home confinement after decades in prison. FBI families, law-enforcement groups, and many Republicans condemned it. Supporters had long called him a political prisoner. This is the closest Biden analogue to Obama’s Oscar López Rivera case. 

https://t.co/G7myA88Fwo

37 federal death-row inmates (commutations to life without parole, December 23, 2024)
Biden spared 37 of 40 people on federal death row. They were not let out. Every one had a murder conviction; one case also involved sexual abuse of the victim. Victims’ families, Trump, and many prosecutors called it a betrayal of justice. Trump later ordered harsher conditions and encouraged states to seek new capital charges. Biden left three on death row: Dylann Roof, Robert Bowers (Tree of Life synagogue), and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Boston Marathon). Two of the 37 even tried to reject the commutation so they could keep appealing.

That’s not “Trump let a child predator out.” That’s you mixing two different cases because one name is convenient.If we’re counting who actually cut time for people already convicted of sex trafficking and child porn, that’s Biden (Jin swap, Graham, Shine, death-row rape-murders taken off the needle). He later pled and got credit for time already served. That is not “Trump commuted a child-sex sentence.”
Jin is not a “wrongfully detained American.” He was a Chinese national sentenced to 8 years for possessing tens of thousands of child-porn images. Biden commuted that sentence so he could be swapped and deported to China instead of serving it here. Clemency for a child-porn convict is still clemency for a child-porn convict, swap or not.
Jackson staying in prison for life is exactly what the original post said. Commuting a death sentence for kidnapping, rape, and murder is still mercy for a rapist-murderer. Same with Avila-Torrez (raped and stabbed two little girls), Gabrion, Basham/Fulks, etc. They are not walking free. They were taken off death row.

If the standard is “did they cut time for people with sex crimes,” Biden did it in the late-term “nonviolent drug” batches too:Lairon Graham: pleaded to fentanyl conspiracy and four counts of sex trafficking by force/coercion. Judge called it one of the most heinous cases he’d seen. Biden cut 22 years to 12½.  
Valentino Shine Sr.: jury convicted him of running a sex-trafficking operation, beating and doping women, three of whom later overdosed. 30 years cut to about 18.

Those men get out years earlier because Biden labeled the cases “drug.”Obama’s record is the same pattern at scale: 1,715 commutations. He also put Oscar López Rivera back on the street — FALN leadership tied to a bombing campaign that killed and maimed civilians. Clinton had already offered him a deal; Obama finished the job.Nobody said every commutation dumps a rapist on the sidewalk the next morning. The point is simple: Obama and Biden repeatedly used clemency to shorten time for people whose records include rape, child porn, sex trafficking, and terrorism-linked violence, then sold it as “nonviolent second chances.” That’s the record. Taake doesn’t erase it.

text:
[The Most Important Question Is: “Who Are You?”]
— What Must Humans Complete After AI?

Recently in South Korea,

discussions have continued

over the possible integration
of the military academies
of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Those in favor

talk about

educational efficiency
and jointness.

Those opposed

talk about

the traditions
and identities

of each branch.

This debate

is not simply

about whether
the academies should be merged.

It raises

a deeper question.

“Who are we?”

──────────────────

AI

connects information rapidly

and expands

many of the capabilities
human beings possess.

As technology advances

and more people gain access
to similar tools,

a new set of questions

becomes increasingly important.

What distinguishes us?

Who am I?

What do we exist for?

These are

questions of identity.

──────────────────

A military

does not become strong

through weapons alone.

What do we exist

to protect?

A shared answer
to that question

creates

organizational cohesion

and standards
for action.

That is why

military identity

is not merely
a matter of tradition.

It is also

an important standard

that determines

what an organization
exists to protect

and how it should act.

──────────────────

This question

is not only
for the military.

What value

will a company
take responsibility for
to the end?

What kind of human beings

will a university
educate?

With what philosophy

will a nation
build its future?

And

why do

human beings exist?

──────────────────

AI

can provide

countless answers.

“Who am I?”

“Why do we exist?”

AI may also

offer answers
to these questions.

But

choosing which answer

will become
your own,

living that answer,

and taking responsibility
for that choice

belong to
human beings.

Perhaps identity

is the continuing answer

to the questions:

Who am I?

And

what do I exist for?

──────────────────

As technology advances,

questions of identity

may become
even more important.

What matters

is not choosing

between technology
and identity.

What will we use

technology for?

In what direction

will we use it?

Those standards

become increasingly important.

Technology

can expand
our capabilities.

But

human beings
must choose

the direction

in which those capabilities
will be used.

──────────────────

1030 Young Stars,

after AI,

as more people gain access

to similar technologies,

there are questions

that become
even more important.

Who am I?

What do I exist for?

AI

can provide

countless answers.

But

choosing an answer,

living it,

and taking responsibility
for it

belong to
human beings.

Who are you?

Your answer
to that question

shapes
your direction.

— Captain Kang Sangbo
Civilization Designer
Commander-in-Chief,
Gaegeunsang United Grand Fleet

text:
The US has opened a financial front against Iran, aimed at the payment channels its naval blockade cannot reach.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the department has launched Operation Economic Outcast to cut off all financial lifelines to the Iranian regime and its enablers, with awards offered for actionable tips from anywhere in the world.

Bessent said the US is "no longer managing the Iranian threat. We are ending it."

The blockade was reinstated on July 14. CENTCOM says 103 commercial vessels have been redirected since it resumed.

US forces destroyed two Iranian small boats on Monday after the IRGC tried to seize a Navy drone in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials told Axios.

Analysts expecting Tehran to absorb this round point to decades of experience with US restrictions and to oil sales settled in yuan with China.

The rial has fallen sharply since the blockade resumed, which analysts read as evidence of lost oil revenue and costlier imports. Iran has no workaround for the blockade itself.

text:
I retired at 20 because I put forth the best effort I could. I took every job offered, had 4.0 marks. 
I was missing a single qualification (Enlisted Surface Warfare Specialist) in the Navy, not because I didn't try for it. Because my Department Head & Division Officer at the time refused permission for me to complete the required training while I was on board the USS Theodore Roosevelt!! 

I was given no recourse it went all the way up the chain to the ships CO, since it wasn't endorsed positively by immediate chain he didn't approve it. 

Back then in the 1980s if you were an E-6 trying for E-7 and had served on a ship in the Navy and then left without that pin you didn't get selected for E7.
I had no choice. I was not selected for E-7 and therefore forced into mandatory retirement as an E6 at 20 years! A few days before my actual retirement I was informed that I could come back as an E-7  because I had finally after been selected! 🙄

By then it just didn't feel worth the effort. I had moved & resettled. It literally didn't feel like a reward for service as much as a token gift to try and keep me around.

text:
Trump Has Untethered Himself From Reality

NYT Gift Article link
Listen · 12:24 min
15SEP2026
By Thomas B. Edsall
https://t.co/9FvU3SWamC
Mr. Edsall contributes a weekly essay from Washington on politics, demographics and inequality.

Last Tuesday, President Trump demonstrated for the few who remain in doubt that his mind is trapped in a fictional world where he is the heroic savior of the nation, if not all mankind.

That day, Trump honored the men and women who braved death or died on Sept. 11, 2001, but most of all he honored himself, portraying himself as willing to lose life or limb during the aftermath of the destruction of the World Trade Center.

Speaking at a Tunnel to Towers Foundation event honoring police officers, firefighters and other first responders, Trump recounted his memory of 9/11 and the days that followed. It has to be read in full to be truly reckoned with.

I want to just thank my people. I took a lot —— I was building a big building in New York, and I took the whole crew down there right after this happened. And they were — they had no hesitation. Everybody went down with me. We went down as a big group of people. Wasn’t too much we could do. I’ll be honest. It was, it was raw.

Nobody had seen anything like it ever. We had other buildings. The United States Steel Building was creaking, really creaking, and we thought it was going to fall down. The truth is, it creaked a lot. It creaked. It still creaks, but it never came down.

And I’ll never forget two firemen. We thought it was coming down on top of us, and two firemen, big strong guys. And I’m not the smallest guy in the world. They grabbed me under the arm, said, “Got to get out of here!” And they literally lifted me up. This is not easy to do. I’m big. They lifted me up and they started running with me. I said, “Fellas, I can run myself.” But they were amazing. But they thought it was coming down. It didn’t come down.

The words were barely out of Trump’s mouth before the challenges to his version of events began.

At 6:30 p.m. that same day, CNN’s Daniel Dale published “Fact Check: Trump’s Story About Being Carried Away by Firefighters After the 9/11 Attack,” which begins:

President Donald Trump has for years told false or unproven stories about what he supposedly saw and did on 9/11 and soon after. As the 25th anniversary of the terror attack approaches, Trump told another story at the White House on Tuesday — in which he claimed to have been carried away by firefighters amid fears of an imminent building collapse at some point after the attack.

It’s possible there are elements of truth in Trump’s latest story, versions of which he has told before, but he hasn’t provided any evidence for it. And some parts of his Tuesday account — which he delivered at an event honoring 9/11 first responders — are misleading at best. He was miles away from the World Trade Center on 9/11 and was not whisked out of any building near ground zero that day.

Trump, New York magazine’s Nia Prater and Chas Danner wrote in “Trump Repeats Disputed Yarn About His 9/11 Role,” “is telling iffy 9/11 stories again.”

The president, Prater and Danner contended, “used his speech to repeat a questionable anecdote about his whereabouts and actions in the aftermath of the tragedy and later defended his recollection as questions arose.”

Trump himself quickly sensed the suspicions questioning the veracity of his comments and posted a defense of his remarks on Truth Social later last Tuesday night:

Everything I said was exactly accurate and, to prove the point, I am attaching clips of me there with numerous of my people, including my then Head of Security, Matthew Calamari, who has confirmed that very sad trip to Lower Manhattan, many times, to many different Journalists, but it’s a story that just won’t die. The Fake News doesn’t want to listen, even when they know their story is false.

Trump acknowledged that he and his crew did not go to ground zero on the same day as the twin towers’ collapse, but claimed “I was there as soon as the Law allowed.”

Twenty-five years ago on Sept. 11, whatever else he was doing later, Trump was four miles away at Trump Tower, where he called into WWOR-TV to say that he could see out one window to the World Trade Center. He also took the time, on a day when nearly 3,000 people died, to mention that a building of his, 40 Wall Street, “was the second-tallest building in downtown Manhattan and it was actually, before the World Trade Center, was the tallest,” as my news-side colleague Katie Rogers noted last Tuesday. “And then,” Trump continued, “when they built the World Trade Center, it became known as the second tallest. And now it’s the tallest.”

As Rogers pointed out, “It wasn’t.”

A 2019 PolitiFact report, “Donald Trump Says He Spent a Lot of Time With 9/11 Responders. Here Are the Facts,” makes perhaps the most damning case against Trump’s claims. PolitiFact interviewed Richard Alles, a New York Fire Department battalion chief on Sept. 11, 2001, to check out similar claims about 9/11 that Trump made earlier:

Alles said he had no knowledge of Trump being at the site or sending 100 or so workers there to help.

“I was in a supervisory role with the Fire Department at the time,” said Alles, who said he was on the scene about 20 minutes after the second building collapsed. “I was there for several months — I have no knowledge of his being down there.”

If Trump had sent a crew of 100 workers, “there would be a record of it. Everybody worked under direct supervision of the Police and Fire Department and the joint commander for emergency services. Is there a chance he was ever down there by himself and I didn’t know it? It’s possible, but I know of no one who ever witnessed him there.”

In a Sept. 9 article, “60 Posts in 10 Hours: How Trump’s Social Media Reflects His Version of Reality,” my colleague in the newsroom Peter Baker provided crucial insight into Trump’s macho, almost fantastical, notion of himself.

Over Labor Day weekend, Baker wrote,

President Trump’s social media account roared to life. In what has increasingly become his weekend habit, he unleashed a daylong barrage of posts that put the bully in the modern bully pulpit.

There were images of Mr. Trump intimidating Canada’s prime minister with a hockey stick, personally bombing enemy targets and patrolling dark streets with killer robots. There were maps showing the United States taking over other countries, and maps renaming a state. text:
I know a lot of people have pointed this out already today, but I want to help drive the point home that there is a difference between 'fully guaranteed money' and 'total guaranteed money'.

'Full Guarantees' is all the money that player is getting no matter what happens after the deal is signed, whether it be injury or something else.

'Total Guarantees' is the total amount of 'guaranteed money' that is on the contract as a whole. What most people don't realize is that a lot of guarantees don't kick in until future seasons via roster bonuses, which only is fully guaranteed if the player is still on the roster by a certain date.

The reported number of the Steelers offering JPJ $33 MM is for what PIT was willing to FULLY guarantee at signing, not the total guarantees over the course of the entire contract.

So when comparing that number to what the other top CBs in the league like Gonzalez & Witherspoon got, the number to compare is their guarantees at signing, not their total guarantees. 

Witherspoon got a little more than $59 MM fully guaranteed & Gonzalez got just under $54 MM fully guaranteed. So that's still a lot more (over $20 MM more) than what PIT was apparently offering to Porter ($33 MM in full guarantees would put Porter at 18th in the league at the CB position), but it's not the $70 MM difference some people think it is becasue they're comparing the offered full guarantees vs. what Witherspoon & Gonzalez got in total guarantees.

I'm guessing Joey is seeking around what Jaycee Horn got on his deal ($46.7 MM fully guaranteed), and frankly, I think that is more than fair given what Porter has done in his first 3 years in the league & Pittsburgh should have given him that to get this deal finalized.

In the end, I'm coming away disappointed that Pittsburgh allowed this to get in the way of locking up Joey for the long haul. I understand they don't love to dish out a high number of full guarantees to players & CB is a pretty volatile position, but the market is the market, and to me, Porter as a legit man-to-man eraser is more than worth paying & investing long-term in.

Hopefully PIT can find a way to still keep Joey in PIT for the long-haul, but if he refuses to play this year without a new contract, a trade could very possibly be coming at some point before the trade deadline.

Although many fairy encounters contain incidences of travelling through the air, and from fairy mound to fairy mound, the occasions where the fairies soar into outer space are few and far between.
This is an often overlooked, and even misrepresented factor when trying to match fairy abductions to UFO encounters.
However, the common links between soul-flight, shamanic journeying, fairy abductions, and, indeed, UFO's, are still tantalising.
Writing in their paper, Small Gods, Small Demons: Remnants of an Archaic Fairy Cult in Central and South-Eastern Europe, Professor Éva Pócs, explains, "The typical fairy communication known from folklore accounts usually takes place in a characteristic space-time structure that is also a form typical of possession by the dead as it appears in this region."
This is an important consideration as a distortion of space-time is often reported by those who have such experiences.
In fact, the trooping fairies sighted by many here in Ireland sounds quite similar, with a flow of airborne lights moving from ancient monument and site to another turning up frequently in our folklore
In this example from Co. Wicklow we have a very definite description of airborne fairy travel.
“At this Rath in Krishuna it is said the fairies gather on certain nights. They ride on the wings of the wind and retreat at cockcrow to the rath of Mullaghmast in Kildare. The people of this neighbourhood are said to keep a black cock in order to defeat the more evil minded of the fairies and to preserve them from harm.”
This fairy wind seems to have the power to carry a person over the threshold between the fairy Otherworld and our own world. Sometimes people describe being transported in strange carriages and even upon brooms. These are lifted in the air and carried faster than seems possible.
The destination, again, is dream-like, often, it seems, deliberately so, as if to mask another reality just below the surface.
"Some time ago men were putting up hay in a field in Cam. A fairy wind came and took away the hay. A man threw his hat after it. He said it was lucky to do that - that the fairy wind wouldn't do any harm, but when the wind settled there was a boy gone with it. One night when the boy's father was going by Pat Cunningham's fort, he heard fairy music, he went into the fort and found the boy."
Robert Kirk, the 17th century Scottish fairy folklorist, also wrote about such "secret paths" which a person might stumble onto and be then led to seeing the fair folk and maybe being captured for a while.
Kirk interesting describes the movement of fairies as "swimming in the air near the earth" which sounds very much like a travelling river of energetic consciousness, or a separate reality, almost.
In his book, Spirit Paths: An exploration of Otherworldly Routes, Paul Devereaux tells us of an 18th century witness to the fairy parade. They describe 'the fairies' as "...leaping and frisking in the air, making a path in the air."
John Keel, the American journalist and writer who studied strange phenomenon speculated that all otherworldly beings emanated from what he termed the 'super-spectrum'. 
This was the range of the electromagnetic spectrum not usually discernable through ordinary human senses.
Keel noticed that many accounts of UFO's, fairies, and demonic beings emerging into our reality were often accompanied by reports of them changing colours before settling on their physical form.
This would sometimes take the form of coloured lights in the sky or the beings seeming to fly out from the rainbow itself.
As Keel writes in his fascinating work, The Eighth Tower, "When men of ancient Greece and Rome saw what we now term UFOs, they noted that the objects changed colours, conforming to the known colour spectrum. So the word specter was born."
Asian shamanistic techniques also use a type of rainbow-path to ascend into the upper worlds in order to contact both ancestor spirits and other forms of consciousness.
In this account from 1671, a woman describes how a fairy asks for her help in delivering a baby and transports the woman upon the wind, "When she returned, she told me, that when she went with the man out at the gate, it seemed to her as if she was carried for a time along in the wind, and so she came to a room, on one side of which was a little dark chamber, in which his wife lay in bed in great agony. My wife went up to her, and, after a little while, aided her till she brought forth the child after the same manner as other human beings. The man then offered her food, and when she refused it, he thanked her, and accompanied her out, and then she was carried along, in the same way in the wind, and after a while came again to the gate, just at ten o'clock."
Form 'The Troll Labour': Thomas Keightley's, The Fairy Mythology, Illustrative of the Romance and Superstition of Various Countries and was published in 1850.
When taken to the Fairy or Spirit Otherworld a person may be chosen to become a healer or communicator between the human and spirit world. One particular way this is achieved is by having magic stones or objects placed inside the persons body.
In terms of parallels between medicine men/ women and the Irish bean feasa, this was deemed to bestow an ability to heal the sick, see future events and deal with ancestral spirits.
Near Dromkeel stone circle in 1992 a local farmer, John McManus, described how he was taken from his home by four small figures. He awoke in a circular ‘room’ where he was given an electric shock and something was put inside him. He then found himself back in his house where the floor was covered in mud and stones.
Three years later McManus had another experience where he felt compelled to walk to his window and watch lights appearing to drift across the nearby mountains.
He felt as if he had been drawn to witness in order to participate.
This is a well documented aspect of fairy lore. In many cases it takes the form of fairies playing a hurling match which they cannot begin until a human interacts with them in some way.
Staying with McManus, this example of an object being placed inside a person is reported in all indigenous cultures when recounting experiences with fairy-type beings. Sometimes the experience takes the form of a person feeling as if they are being cut into pieces only to be put together again. In other examples the object placed in the body becomes the instigator of new healing knowledge or psychopomp abilities.
There is no requirement to deny the physicality of what has taken place except in contemporary Western culture.
Writing in Aboriginal Men of High Degree, A.P. Elkin describes an Australian Aboriginal account of a medicine man taken by 'spirits' into the sky world where an operation is performed on him by having quartz crystals inserted into his side. He could henceforth visit the sky and establish communication with the sky spirits and even be summoned by them.
The Aboriginal tribes of The Southern Murray region reflect the same beliefs as other Australian indigenous people which they say have been passed down in oral form for over 60'000 years.
Aboriginal cave art depicting these encounters with the sky-serpent spirits have been dated to at least 40'000 BCE.
Returning to Ireland, this account recorded in 1926 is interesting, “I was learning to speak Irish at the time. A gang of us would be sent over beyond Lough Gara every week to be taught by the master there.
Some of us would go on bicycles and would often cycle home in the dark.
We were nervous when we’d cycle by the lake as we would often see three lights skimming across the water. Sometimes the lights would appear in the trees at the lake edge and other times they would submerge beneath the water.
Our parents put the lights down to the work of God.
‘Don’t worry about them, they’re only lost souls trying to get into heaven. They’re no harm.’”
The only frame of reference at the time was religion and lost souls, which in most cases was short-hand for fairies.
This account from Wentzs's The Fairy Faith in Celtic Countries describes another airborne fairy encounter with multiple possible interpretations: "As they approached Listowel the doctor writes that he witnessed what he thought was the light of a house about a half mile ahead of him. On approach, though, the light began to behave in a very mysterious manner, “Moving up and down, to and fro, diminishing to a spark, then expanding into a yellow, luminous flame.”
As they rode on, the doctor and his companion then saw two further lights behaving in a similarly bizarre fashion.
The doctor tells us that the lights were six feet high and four feet wide and within each one was, “…a radiant being having human form.”
The two lights then glided towards each other until they touched and the beings inside were able to walk between each light as if it was one individual orb.
Many Irish fairy encounters not only describe the fairies moving through the air but an entire fairy mound itself, which is seen to light up and spin, and at other times a parade of lights are seen to emanate from it and take off across the sky. This aspect has been documented at the rath situated near Keadeen, Co. Wicklow.
In this example the lights also seem to foretell of a death.
"One night about three years ago the Hartnetts who lived in Gardenfield were going to the fair in Drom and they saw a bright light shining over near Mrs. Dowling's house. They said to themselves that it was very early Mrs. Dowling was up. Mrs. Dowling saw the same light that night moving up around Harnett's house then it came down and it went into the fort and disappeared. That happened before Mr. Harnett's death."

text:
America is failing because we abandoned moral clarity.

Congress, ignoring this is treason.

The real threat to American chip manufacturing wasn't China — 

it was American politicians. They created tax laws and trade policies that made it financially stupid to manufacture here, forcing companies to offshore. The threat assessment teams saw it coming, but politicians didn't understand technology and didn't care. Now we're paying the price with memory shortages while AI demand explodes. The enemy was never overseas. It was always in Washington.

.....................................................................................................

It's extremely dangerous:

This isn't just about memory chips anymore. The same political decisions that hollowed out our manufacturing base are now creating a real national security risk. If we can't produce our own advanced memory and chips, we're completely dependent on foreign supply chains for the technology that will power AI, defense systems, and the entire future economy. That's not sustainable.

......................................................................................................

The reason we have so many issues is because almost every AI box and accelerator — 

AMD's MI300X/MI325X, NVIDIA's DGX Spark, and AMD's Gorgon Halo — is designed in the US but manufactured in Taiwan by TSMC. 

Very few companies are actually building these chips in America. 

The only real exception is Groq's inference chips, which are made in upstate New York. Everything else comes from Taiwan or gets final assembly through Taiwanese companies. 

That's the core problem.America falls behind China in AI development because we can't get enough memory chips.

The US military becomes dangerously dependent on foreign chips for weapons systems.

AI companies move their headquarters and talent out of America to countries that can actually supply the hardware.

We face repeated supply chain crises and massive price spikes every time AI demand grows.

National security gets compromised because critical AI infrastructure stays reliant on Taiwan and China.

.........................................................................................................

The real threat to American chip manufacturing wasn't China —

it was American politicians who made it unprofitable to build here. Now China is flooding the market with AI accelerators and memory chips from companies like Huawei, Cambricon, Alibaba T-Head, Baidu Kunlunxin, Moore Threads, Biren, MetaX, Enflame, Iluvatar CoreX, CXMT, and YMTC. We offshored our future, and they're happy to fill the gap.

.......................................................................................................

Here are eight real solutions:

Change the tax code to give massive deductions for any company building and manufacturing chips in America.

Fast-track permitting and slash the red tape for new semiconductor fabs.

Create targeted tariffs on Chinese AI chips and memory while we rebuild our own capacity.

Offer government grants and low-interest loans specifically for domestic chip production.

Fund vocational training programs to build a skilled American semiconductor workforce.

Require all critical military and government AI systems to use American-made chips within five years.

Create a national semiconductor strategy with clear goals and accountability, not just another spending bill.

Partner with allies like Japan, South Korea, and the Netherlands to diversify supply chains away from Taiwan and China.

....................................................................................................

Here are five key bills and constitutional measures that need to be passed:

American Semiconductor Sovereignty Act — This law would permanently require all critical military, government, and AI infrastructure to use chips manufactured in the United States. 
It must be written so no future president or Congress can weaken or repeal it without a supermajority vote, preventing politicians from playing politics with our national security every four years.

Domestic Chip Manufacturing Tax Credit Act — A permanent tax credit that heavily rewards companies for building and producing chips in America, making it financially impossible for them to offshore again.

American Semiconductor Workforce Act — This would fund and create new specialized trade schools and vocational programs focused on semiconductor manufacturing, chip design, and advanced fabrication to build a skilled American workforce.

Critical Technology Protection Act — A law that blocks tax breaks or government contracts for any company that moves advanced manufacturing overseas, with automatic penalties.

Constitutional Amendment for American Industrial Sovereignty — A new amendment to the Constitution that protects American manufacturing and technological independence from political manipulation. It would explicitly prevent both Democrats and Republicans from ever again selling out American industry for short-term political gain, codifying into the highest law of the land that our critical industries must remain under American control to protect future generations of citizens.

........................................................................................

Congress, America’s dependence on foreign manufacturing — 

from China to Europe and beyond —

 is no longer a policy failure. It is a national security emergency. Democrats and the DSA have become an active threat to our survival, while too many RINOs look the other way. The damage from 2021 to 2024 was only the beginning. If you refuse to act, the crisis ahead will make a black swan event look small. We must reach 60% American-made by 2036 and 70% by 2046 — everything grown, mined, manufactured, and processed here. The future of this country is on the line.

........................................................................................................

America is failing because we abandoned moral clarity. 

A nation without God in its leaders has no compass. Democrats, DSA, and self-serving politicians now put lobbyists and China ahead of American citizens. When those in power answer only to themselves, they betray both the people and their oath. This is why we’re losing our country.

@JDVance
@Jim_Jordan
@tedcruz
@RepLuna 
@SenatorMikeLee

text:
First, I would like to thank @MikeInganamort for being the only New Jersey official representative at the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight hearing, "Restoring Election Integrity: Oversight of Voter Fraud in New Jersey".

This House investigation that was today, September 15, 2026 was on New Jersey's "software glitch" involving voter registration.  The Sherrill administration would not allow *any state official* to show or testify.

@Congressman_JVD  thank you for holding this hearing.  Please take this "Software Glitch" investigation as far as you possibly can and hold all accountable.  We citizens of New Jersey need your help.

@Congressman_JVD recognized himself for making the opening statement of this hearing.  His statement needs it's own highlighting.

@Congressman_JVD, This was very well said.  Thank you.

Welcome everyone here today for this subcommittee on Oversight and Judiciary. 

Today's hearing is an important one. It's important for every American who still believes their vote is supposed to count for something.

States like New Jersey have decided that the well being of illegal immigrants, in my opinion, is more important than the well being of American citizens.

Evidence of this can be seen, and I'm going to digress for a minute. Bear with me. Paints a picture. Evidence of this can be seen all over my home state, which is a self proclaimed Sanctuary State. On August 28th, a 9 month old boy was killed in a grocery store parking lot in Jackson, New Jersey. The driver who struck him had no license, no legal status in the country, and a final order of removal that nobody in the state ever enforced.

Governor Sherrill had announced $20.2 million to fund illegal immigrants, some of them criminals, to fund a legal defense fund for them.

Are American taxpayers now going to cover? And that's the question you ask.

Are they actually going to cover some of the legal defense of the two that killed those two toddlers in the in the last month? I guess we'll find out.

Nine days ago, a six year old girl was kidnapped out of her own bed in Warren County, New Jersey. Kidnapped, taken out of her home, and sexually assaulted.

Anybody that has children or grandchildren, I think, can feel that pain. Six years old. Six year old little girl sexually assaulted, ripped out of her bedroom at home. The man charged in that attack is again in the country illegally.

Why was he allowed to be here? Why was he allowed anywhere near that little girl? Why are the citizens of New Jersey forced to ask these questions after the damage is already done? Why are the citizens of New Jersey forced to pay for this?

Whose side is New Jersey government on?
Because it's not the side of that nine month old little boy, and it wasn't the side of that six month little girl.

And that's the question hanging over this entire hearing, the whole deal.

Whose side are you on? What the hell is going on in our state and in our country? What was going on? What are the recent impacts of states offering sanctuary to people that are not citizens of this great country? But the reason we're meeting here today goes even deeper. So, one of the most fundamental and precious and important rights of Americans, and that's voting.

And it's more than even just letting violent criminals walk our streets.

There is a coordinated effort to provide government documentation to these people and throw out the sanctity of our great elections by allowing them to register to vote. This hearing is going to examine how roughly over 6,000 new citizens, no I'm sorry, noncitizens, not new citizens, I wish they were. How over 6,000 noncitizens were registered to vote in the great state of New Jersey between June 2023, June 2024, how approximately 400 noncitizens successfully voted in our elections during that time and almost 7,000 were registered. That we know of. That we know of. Quite frankly, we know there's more. Democrat New Jersey Governor Mikey Cheryl held a press conference on July 21, 2026, claiming that these improper  voter registrations were the result of a system error. So, let's take that apart.

Let's look into it. During that press conference, Sherrill blamed the softway vendor and the former Democratic New Jersey Governor Phil Murphy.

There's still a lot, a real lot that we don't know about how this happened and why it took so long for the public to learn about it to date. Just some of the things we don't know what elections these non citizens voted in federal, state or local.   And it matters. You know, anybody knows if you follow local elections, it can be a handful of votes very often. It can even happen in Congress. But certainly at the local level, five votes, 10 votes, three votes, they can make a big difference.

400 votes can make a big difference. How the state government let this happen in the first place? Why didn't New Jersey immediately remove these noncitizens from the voter roles the moment it found out? And why New Jersey waited two full years to tell the American public about any of this? two years.

New Jersey knew in 2024. They knew in 2024. They knew in 2025. They knew in 2026.

And it wasn't corrected until 2026 when the pressure was on from the Department of Homeland Security. And their back was against the wall. But 2024, nothing happened. They knew, didn't do anything about it. 2025 they knew didn't do anything about it. 2026 they knew didn't do anything about it. Didn't inform the public.

Didn't clean the rolls up until they were forced to just held it there. Ladies and gentlemen, in political terms, that's called a cover up. It means you don't want people to know what's really going on. So, what don't we know? We don't know what elections these noncitizens voted in federal, state, or local. We don't know how the state government let this happen in the first place. We don't know why New Jersey didn't. Immediately, if you found out mistakes can happen, it's okay. Mistakes happen. But you correct the mistakes. You clean up the mistakes immediately, as quickly as possible. You don't let them to continue to vote in primary elections, in general elections over multiple years.

Why did they wait two full years to tell the American public? And we don't even know and we can talk about today if 6,600 is the real number. It could be higher. These are people. The 6,600 are people who admitted they weren't legal citizens but wanted to vote. I don't know how many folks might be out there that didn't admit they were illegal citizens, got their driver's license, and said they also wanted a vote.

This committee, in coordination with the House Administration Committee, launched an investigation into the egregious case of improper voter registrations. We sent letters to New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Dave Caldwell and I've spoken to him. He has been somewhat cooperative, but now he is undergoing his own internal investigation in the state of New Jersey. 

And IDEMIA requesting the documents that would show how this happened in an election system that is supposed to be fair and free. It's America. IDEMIA has cooperated. We've met with them. We've talked with them numerous times. New Jersey has done everything it can not to cooperate and stonewall the investigation. 

I sent another letter to the governor, It was a polite letter. It was an informed letter asking for information. It wasn't a political letter and we got a very, very political letter back with no information. Now, thanks to IDEMIA, the software company, we know that the alleged system error was not an issue on IDEMIA's end, but rather an issue prompted by the state of New Jersey. 

Internal documents show that New Jersey government tested and approved the spec specifications for the IDEMIA software that allowed these illegals to be registered between 2023 and 2026. They tested it. They approved it. They allowed it.

We also know that 2024, IDEMIA received a request from New Jersey after the state finally realized that noncitizens were being registered to vote. So they put in a request to IDEMIA. That means they knew. 

Ladies and gentlemen, they knew in 2024 and then for two years crickets, nothing happened.

Just kept on going, kept on voting, kept on doing the same old thing. No public warning, no accounting, no investigations, no information for the voters of New Jersey. Just silence.

Republicans forced their hand. That's unfortunate. And by the way, somebody said, "Well, some of the people that may be voting could be Republicans that some of them are Republicans." I don't care.

If they're not legal, they shouldn't be voting. No matter if they're a Republican or a Democrat or independent, they shouldn't be voting.

This problem exposes real loopholes in federal law, including the National Voter Registration Act, which requires states to offer voter registration materials to people applying for driver's licenses. That's okay, but not for people that are illegals and some cases illegal criminals.

Since 2023, 19 states in Washington DC have allowed noncitizens to apply for and obtain driver's licenses and with that access to voter registration materials. Some states even go further and allow noncitizens to vote in local elections. These factors combined with weak voter role maintenance have made improper registrations like this one more likely, not less likely. I guarantee you, I'll bet anybody anything. If we looked everywhere in the country; and especially some of the states, we'd find a whole lot more. 

At the start of his second term, the President signed two executive orders imposing criminal penalties for noncitizen voting and giving the Department of Homeland Security and other agencies access for verification.

Thank goodness he did, whether you like it or not, because it allowed DHS and secretary to go shed light on the mess. And it forced the public revelation that had been covered up that illegal people had voted in elections and had registered thousands of them.

This committee is going to do everything it can to continue getting to the bottom of how this was allowed to happen. It's simple. Only it really is simple.

Only Americans should vote in American elections. Not complicated. It's just as simple that American children should be safe in a grocery store parking lot where they should be safe in their own beds where they should be safe walking to school. They should be safe on the streets, in their homes, in their vehicles. They should be safe. It's America.

It shouldn't be what I'm saying now, honest to God, shouldn't be a partisan statement. You heard me say if a Republican is illegally registered, they shouldn't be voting either. It should be the entire point of government to protect national security, our own security.

So, I'm going to ask one more time as we sit here and think about this, whose side are we on? 

I know the side. I believe I know the side this committee, or at least the majority of this committee is on. I would like New Jersey to finally tell us all the information whose side it is on too? If there is nothing to hide; if there is nothing to see, there should be no problem.

Just turn it over. Let the sun shine in.

Let the light come and let's find out.

text:
Carney eyes ‘unique alliance’ with EU, but there are legal limits to his plan
Story by Tracy Moran

OTTAWA — Prime Minister Mark Carney has suggested that deeper integration and a “unique alliance” between Canada and the European Union (EU) could be the answer to the souring of the Canada-U.S. relationship amid the trade war with U.S. President Donald Trump.

“We’re not looking to become a member of the European Union ,” he said on Sunday.

“What we are looking — and will begin discussions for — [is] a unique alliance with the European Union. We share the same values, we have the same priorities, and we have very complementary strengths.”

Strategically, Canada offers Europe a like-minded G7 partner with natural resources, defence capacity, and similar values — as well as a shared interest in being less dependent upon an increasingly unpredictable Washington. But the policy content of Carney’s proposal remains undefined — and scholars on EU law say that the EU has no ready-made legal route for granting Canada a membership-like status.

Under Carney especially, Canada is a “key player” and “highly respected,” said Cambridge professor Catherine Barnard, who specializes in EU law.

But trade watchers are also skeptical that Carney’s gambit for a “ unique alliance ” will lead to a new formal, membership-like arrangement anytime soon. The first hurdle is that no such EU category currently exists.

When asked what a “unique alliance” might look like, Barnard said nobody knows and pointed to the difference between the political and legal dimensions.

“The EU wants to be close to Canada and supportive of Canada — that’s the political side,” she said.

Legally, however, “there is just no possibility (of that) as the EU stands,” she said, pointing to the Michel Barnier staircase of the available models. At the top is full membership, followed by looser forms of economic integration — European Economic Area (EEA) participation, Swiss-style bilateral accords, customs-union arrangements, and free-trade agreements. Canada is already on the bottom step with the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), an EU-Canada free-trade agreement provisionally in place since 2017.

Simon Usherwood, professor of politics and international studies at The Open University, also pointed to the lack of “off-the-shelf relationships with other countries.”

While Carney has said he’s not seeking it, full membership would simply not be feasible under the EU treaties as they stand.

“People jokingly say, ‘Oh, yes, Canada could join, join the EU,’” Barnard said. “Well, legally that’s impossible because Article 49 of the treaty says you’ve got to be a European state, and Canada is not that.”

Even if the focus is just on a bespoke partnership, the political room for this remains uncertain as it’s not just a question of what Canada hopes to obtain but also what privileges — and demands — the EU is willing to extend to Ottawa.

The EU could, in theory, devise a new arrangement for a country it wants to draw closer. But Barnard said Brussels would be wary of creating a precedent because any generous concession to Canada could prompt Britain, Switzerland, the EEA states, Ukraine and other countries outside the bloc to demand comparable treatment.

Grégoire Roos, director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House, was more enthusiastic about institutional innovation and said the debate about Canada comes at an interesting time — when the EU is considering whether to create more flexible, intermediate forms of association.

“Europe is asking itself where it wants to go in terms of enlargement,” he said, noting that it will depend on whether the EU is willing to create a broader set of intermediate relationships between full membership and outsider status.

While a bigger relationship with Canada could upset other countries, Roos argued that the risks of institutional innovation should not deter Europe.

“In the realm of politics and policymaking, any kind of audacity is risky. But this is exactly what Europe needs,” he said.

But if a new formal status is unlikely anytime soon, what exactly can Ottawa and Brussels achieve?

On that point, the experts agree that the clearest — and least legally questionable — way forward is on defence, Ukraine support, and industrial cooperation.

Usherwood, for example, expects Canada’s support for Ukraine to continue to expand and believes its participation in Security Action for Europe (SAFE), the EU’s defence financing programme, could “bear some fruit pretty quickly on defence procurements.”

Both the EU and Canada have incentives given U.S. unpredictability and the need to diversify their defence supply chains.

Other areas for strategic cooperation could include critical minerals, energy security — including potential undersea electricity interconnections — and technology.

Carney has also suggested that a deal could include greater mobility for Canadians, specifically “enhanced labour mobility… enhanced educational opportunities, enhanced research co-operation.”

Usherwood said a youth-mobility scheme would be more realistic than unrestricted free movement. But Barnard cautioned that EU member states would retain control over admission numbers and could, in principle, set Canadian quotas at zero.

Roos was more optimistic and said freer movement for Canadians to work and live in the EU would not be difficult in practical or political terms. He even believes Canada’s positive image in Europe could help mute populist opposition to such mobility arrangements, at least for now.

When it comes to deeper trade integration between Canada and the EU, however, the experts were more cautious.

Usherwood said CETA itself illustrates how difficult deeper integration can be.

“CETA … is still not fully in effect because we’ve still got 10 member states that haven’t done the ratification because they’re worried about access of Canadian agricultural imports into the EU,” he said.

The EU can readily make separate agreements with Canada on defence and security, Barnard said. But WTO rules generally prevent Brussels from offering Canada selective preferential access to parts of the EU market without extending the same treatment to other WTO members. The principal exception is a free-trade agreement or customs union under GATT Article XXIV, which must cover “substantially all” trade between the parties — not a narrow, Canada-specific economic arrangement.

Even if a more generous arrangement were legally feasible, Barnard said, the politics would remain difficult. If Brussels devised a new Canada-specific relationship, countries with stronger geographic or accession claims could demand comparable treatment.

“It’s difficult to see quite what cozy relationship the EU might have with Canada unless they invent something new,” Barnard said. “And if they invent something new, then Ukraine, Bosnia, Serbia, the U.K. all will say, ‘Well, we want some of that, and we have much greater claim than Canada does because we’re on the EU borders.’”

For that reason, Barnard and Usherwood see the “unique alliance” language as more rhetorical than immediately realistic.

text:
Leftists call Tom Tiffany a “pedophile protector” so I asked Grok: “Did Tom Tiffany vote to block the release of the Epstein Files?”

Per Grok:

No. Tom Tiffany voted for the bill that required the Justice Department to release the Epstein files. 
On November 18, 2025, the House passed H.R. 4405, the Epstein Files Transparency Act, 427–1. Tiffany voted yes. Only Rep. Clay Higgins (R-LA) voted no. The Senate passed it by unanimous consent the same day, and it became law. Tiffany issued a statement supporting “full transparency” and criticizing Democrats for keeping the files sealed under Biden. 

Democratic critics (including WisDems and local party posts) point to two earlier party-line procedural votes:
•  July 15, 2025: Tiffany voted yes on H.Res. 580, a rule for other bills. Democrats had tried to use an amendment or related maneuver to force consideration of an Epstein release measure; Republicans defeated those efforts.
•  September 3, 2025: Tiffany voted yes on H.Res. 672 (212–208). An amendment offered by Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA) to immediately bring up H.R. 4405 failed as part of the rule process. Tiffany was among the Republican majority that adopted the rule without that provision. 
He also did not co-sponsor the original Massie-Khanna bill or sign the discharge petition that later forced the November floor vote.
These were standard majority-control votes on how legislation comes to the floor, not recorded votes against the substance of releasing the files. When the bill itself came up, Tiffany supported it. The “voted three times to block” framing is a partisan characterization of the procedural delays, not a description of his vote on the actual transparency legislation.

Justin Bieber and Harry Styles are reportedly among the artists Roc Nation wants for the Super Bowl 2027 Halftime Show. According to TMZ, neither artist has been officially approached yet, and both are unlikely to accept the offer if they are eventually asked to perform.

Roc Nation, which partners with the NFL and serves as the league’s “live music entertainment strategist,” plays a key role in selecting the Halftime Show performer, with Jay-Z having the final say.

Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The NFL typically announces the Halftime Show performer in late September, meaning an announcement could be just weeks away.

The NFL does not pay artists to perform at the Super Bowl Halftime Show. Artists typically take the opportunity for its massive global exposure, which can also lead to increased streaming numbers and ticket sales, particularly when they have new music to promote.

If approached, Justin Bieber would already have experience performing on a major global sporting stage, having recently been involved in the halftime performance at the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final.

Meanwhile, Harry Styles has just announced his “Together, Together Tour 2027,” which will begin in May 2027 and span 12 cities with 25 shows.

The last time the Super Bowl was held at SoFi Stadium, in 2022, the Halftime Show featured Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, Kendrick Lamar and 50 Cent.

text:
The Blame Game

Santa Monica's tourism failed from the inside out. Every excuse offered, COVID, remote work, tariffs, the economy, hit every beach city in Southern California. Anaheim, San Diego, Santa Barbara, Marina del Rey, and Long Beach all took the same hits and came back stronger:

Anaheim: 26.3 million visitors in 2024, 26.5 million in 2025 (up 0.8%).

San Diego: 32.5 million in 2024, 32.8 million in 2025 (up 0.9%).

Santa Barbara: 7.4 million in 2024, 7.5 million in 2025 (up 1.4%).

Marina del Rey: 1.046 million in 2024, 1.056 million in 2025 (up 1.0%), with economic impact rising from $617 million to $636.7 million.

Long Beach: 8.1 million downtown visitors in 2024 (up 2% year over year, within 5% of 2019 levels).

Santa Monica: 4.2 million visitors in 2024, 3.9 million in 2025 (down 7.1%), from 8.7 million at its peak (2017).

The difference isn't the factors. It's the response. While neighbors rebuilt, Santa Monica pointed fingers, at the economy, and let downtown vacancies, homelessness, and crime concerns fester.

Hotel revenue is finally ticking up, and visitor spending rose nearly 9% in 2025 to almost a billion dollars, driven by higher-spending international travelers. But even with the World Cup this year, we still did not surpass our peak tourism. Projections show visitor volume will not pass 2019 levels until 2027 at the earliest, and still won't surpass our peaks until after the Olympics.

Our current leadership needs to own this or step out of the way. Self-accountability means stopping the blame game and fixing what's broken on their watch.

Here's what I'd do differently. I'd push for a dedicated tourism recovery task force with real authority, not another study. I'd fast-track the empty storefronts on the Third Street Promenade with temporary pop-ups and reduced fees for local businesses. And I'd tie city contracts to measurable downtown recovery benchmarks. If the numbers don't move, the contracts don't renew.

I know we can do better. A Higher Standard for Santa Monica 

Derrick Townsend for Santa Monica 2026

The Fundamentals
The primary driver in this matchup is a starting pitching advantage for Kansas City when it comes to limiting traffic on the basepaths. Michael Wacha brings a very strong 3.25 ERA and a 1.11 WHIP to the mound over a large 182-inning sample. On the other side, Houston's Hunter Brown has pitched reasonably well (3.52 ERA) but allows noticeably more baserunners with a 1.30 WHIP. 

While the Astros have the superior overall roster (75-75 vs 66-84) and home-field advantage, the game is being played in a controlled dome environment (roof closed). In a neutral setting without weather variables, Wacha's ability to consistently limit walks and hits gives the Royals a very realistic path to keeping this game tight and pulling off the upset. 

My Probability
Given Wacha's edge in WHIP and stability, I make Kansas City winning this game about a 45% probability. Houston is rightfully favored at home, but the gap on the mound makes this closer than the records suggest.

The Value & Best Execution

Sportsbook: Royals +139 (41.8% break-even)

With my read at 45% and the book's fair value at 40%, there is a solid ~5 points of edge on Kansas City as the road underdog. text:
Scientists discovered a biological “off-switch” for glioblastoma, one of the deadliest brain cancers.

Glioblastoma is widely feared for its aggressive nature and notorious ability to withstand heavy doses of radiation and chemotherapy. 

Historically, these tumors survive by maintaining rapid growth signals and repairing treatment-related DNA damage, leaving patients with extremely limited long-term options. 

However, researchers at The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center have identified a critical weakness in this survival mechanism. Their study focused on PP2A, a natural regulatory enzyme that suppresses cancer-promoting signals, which glioblastoma cells actively deactivate using a shield of proteins, including one known as SET.

In preclinical experiments, scientists found that suppressing the SET protein successfully restored the cancer-fighting activity of PP2A, preventing glioblastoma tumors from forming altogether. Furthermore, disrupting related protective proteins, ANP32A and CIP2A, dramatically increased the sensitivity of cancer cells to radiation therapy. 

Rather than replacing existing treatments, this innovative approach is designed to weaken the tumor's defenses from within, making conventional chemotherapy and radiation far more lethal to the cancer. While clinical trials in humans are still ahead, this discovery offers a vital roadmap toward finally overcoming treatment resistance in one of medicine's most devastating diseases.

source: Palanichamy, K., & Chakravarti, A. (2026). Endogenous inhibitors of PP2A activate oncogenic and DNA damage response kinases in glioblastoma. Cancer Letters.

text:
November 30, 2013. The Iron Bowl. Auburn and No. 1 Alabama tied at 28, one second left on the clock.

Alabama lined up for a 57-yard field goal to win it. Nick Saban had just talked the officials into putting that final second back on the board to try it.

The kick came up short. And standing in the back of his own end zone, nine yards deep, was an Auburn cornerback named Chris Davis.

He caught it and ran.

109 yards later, Jordan-Hare Stadium came apart. Fans poured onto the field from every direction. Auburn won 34-28. It was the first walk-off missed-field-goal return for a touchdown in the history of college football, and it sent Auburn to the SEC Championship and then to the national title game.

Auburn's radio voice, the late Rod Bramblett, delivered the call that's been replayed a million times since. "There goes Davis. Davis is gonna run it all the way back."

They call it the Kick Six. It's the most famous play in Auburn history and one of the most famous in the history of the sport. The grounds crew at Jordan-Hare once painted the exact path of Davis' 109-yard run onto the field, just as a reminder to recruits walking through.

This weekend, one of those recruits was his son.

CJ Davis III is a four-star running back, a junior at Spain Park High School in Birmingham, and he was in Auburn for the Tigers' home opener against Southern Miss. He's held an Auburn offer since middle school, and he's been on that campus more times than he can count.

He left impressed, and put Auburn in his top three.

"Great atmosphere and a great win. It looked like something that I can be a part of and get used to."

He's class of 2028, so he's got a long way to go before he decides anything, and he could end up somewhere else entirely.

But for one Saturday night, the son of the man who ran 109 yards into Auburn immortality stood in that same stadium, on a field that still has his father's footsteps painted into its history, and pictured himself playing there.

Some places just stay in a family.

text:
Charania already reported interest from Detroit and Minnesota previously.

I never thought they’d be actual destinations that Leonard would be willing to consider, but their trade packages would’ve been a lot tougher to form.

Perhaps, with how things have gone with Duren now, the Pistons would’ve been willing to offer him in a sign-and-trade with LA, but I still think that’s unlikely. They wouldn’t have offered Ausar Thompson either so that package becomes “meh” very quickly. 

Minnesota’s package is interesting. There’s a possibility it would’ve been similar to the LaMelo Ball package— Naz Reid and a bunch of swaps. I don’t think Gobert or McDaniels would’ve been on the table. In hindsight, this package is also worse than what LA got from Toronto. But you could also argue that, if Minnesota was willing to push the trade through before the investigation was completed, LA might’ve been able keep some of their picks because Silver seemed hesitant to take away picks that were tied in swaps. At best, Minnesota’s package would’ve taken a serious hit with LA being unable to trade for swaps and there’d be a mid-September bidding war for a newly acquitted Leonard.

text:
This feels as much speculative as it is reassuring. And there are several other important points:

There seems to be a common assumption that he can just be bought—“Make him an offer he can’t refuse.” What makes anyone think he won’t be offered enough to make him happy to stay home?

It won’t surprise anyone if it’s the most ever offered to a Mississippi State player, maybe near the top in the SEC. Coveted players have chosen to stay home, Josh Hubbard and Ace Reese come to mind. And some have left, although certainly none ever with this unprecedented appeal.

And, if you’ve seen the background, you get the impression that what matters to him and his family is not which school and program offers the most money, it’s which school offers them the most…happiness, which is a compound factor.

He can stay home and get to the NFL. Dak Prescott played his position, Jeffery Simmons was from the same home town and high school. He can win awards, if that’s what he’s in it for. People in that talent level have unique motivations.

But when you watch him, and his half hour feature story, you scratch your head at the boorish and arrogant suggestions that all it takes is a check. It could even be considered that you’re insulting him and his family with the assumption that he can simply be flipped and bought for mere money. The meter is running, no, it’s spinning now.

However, thanks but no thanks has been the answer, many times to many offers.

He may leave. If he does, it will be his decision, and you would think that somehow, his beliefs will have changed that he can’t really accomplish all his goals by staying home. Right now, there’s little indication of that and something he once said to his mother pops its head up, that he believed he could be the one to make a difference.

People who’ve never been in that position, where they could make a difference of that magnitude, have a hard time understanding the logic of just not being auction fodder. Maybe it’s too complex to fathom eating as much cake as it takes to satisfy you and having it too. As the saying goes, why not both?

Instead, I've exhausted my savings, accumulated credit card debt, and reached a point where I had to create a Fund just to keep going while I continue searching for work.

If you've ever wondered whether someone can do everything they're supposed to do and still end up in crisis, I'm living it.

So today, I'm asking for your help.

❤️ If you know of a remote full-time, contract, or freelance opportunity, I'd be incredibly grateful for an introduction.

🔁 If you can't help directly, please share or repost this. You never know who might see it.

🙏 And if you're in a position to support my fund, any amount helps me stay afloat while I keep fighting to rebuild my career.

I still believe the right opportunity is out there.

I just need it to reach me before I run out of time.

The Fundamentals
The primary driver in this matchup is a massive starting pitching and situational advantage for San Diego. Walker Buehler takes the mound for the Padres, and while his 4.61 ERA isn't elite, he is significantly more reliable than Colorado's Kyle Freeland (6.37 ERA, 1.46 WHIP, .296 opponent average). 

More importantly, Freeland is returning from the 15-day IL (neck) to make his first start in nearly a month. Having thrown just 47 pitches in his recent rehab start, he will almost certainly be on a strict pitch count tonight. In the high-altitude, run-friendly environment of Coors Field (O/U 11), an early exit from a struggling starter means exposing a weak Rockies bullpen for the majority of the game. Add in the fact that Colorado might be without their home run leader Hunter Goodman (thumb), and the Padres' superior roster (82-68 vs 55-95) is in a prime position to capitalize.

*(Note on continuity: Yesterday I backed the Padres in this matchup and it resolved right. Today is a fresh setup with different pitchers, but the data points to an even stronger situational edge for San Diego given Freeland's limitations.)*

My Probability
Given Freeland's pitch count restrictions exposing the bullpen early in Coors Field, and the massive overall roster gap, I make San Diego winning this game about a 66% probability. 

The Value & Best Execution
Polymarket: Padres 65¢ (65% implied)
Sportsbook: Padres -200 (66.7% break-even)

With my read at 66% and the book's fair value at 63.8%, there is a marginal ~2-point edge on San Diego. If you want to back the Padres, Polymarket's 65¢ offers slightly better execution than laying the steep -200 moneyline at the traditional sportsbook (which requires a 66.7% break-even rate).

Yes, 80% of Indians can eat meat. How many can afford regularly, that is another question.

As time goes by this % will increase since many youngsters fr traditionally vegetarian families eat it. In fact, if you survey today's GenZ TAMBRAM, anecdotally, I doubt if even 20% is genuinely vegetarian. 

And we all know which section of population is growing fastest, even before illegal immigration.

What this does to environment, if every Indian consumes as much as typical American is a different topic for different day.

###  But the question is, how much is Indian cuisine connected to meat, among global audience? 

Yes, we have biriyani. Which, according to our Stalinist left "historians", is  Mughal, hence not even Indian -its Mongol or Turkish or whatever. It is not our copyright. In fact, Pilaf is a very popular Iran dish. Variations exist in practically every country to our west. We have ZERO rights to call any of them Indian. In fact, you will be shot down by the very liberals that scream loudest over #BRICS menu!

We have tandoor and kebab, which again is more of Afghan/Pakistani, product of the dry desert culture.

They may use "Indian" in their signboards for practical reasons given Pak image.  That doesn't make it Indian!

Point is, for good meat dishes there's dozens of choices among Asian/global cuisine! India is probably way down in the list of any meat loving non-Indian.

If a westerner or foreigner wants to eat good meat dish they can choose from these - all of them are highly popular. 

Personally I love all of these except the beef based dishes which I avoid.

- Japanese Sushi, sashimi
- Chinese pork or seafood dishes, steamed fish in sauce and zillion others
- Thai curries with chicken or sea food like Tom Yam
- Viet Pho noodles in beef broth
- Japanese Ramen in pork broth
- Japanese high end beef like Wagyu or black pork
- Pilaf and other Iranian dishes
- Turkish or Iran kebab and other such dishes
- Takoyaki, Yakitori, Satay and other skewered meat dishes from Japan, Malaysia etc.
- Korean beef dishes, bulgogi etc
- Lebanese or Turkish dishes with mild and Mediterranean spices & flavours.
- Padang and many other Indonesian cuisine

Not just that, in most Asian countries, concept of vegetarian is almost non existent. Cambodia, Indonesia, Vietnam and others. It is a modern fad esp among western tourists, so availability is improving with faux native dishes (vegetarian pho or tom yum - eeew!) but its not native. Most locals don't eat that shit.

I am not even going into rest of the world cuisine. As we belong to Asia.

What I am coming to is, IF there is ANYTHING at all about cuisine that INDIA and INDIANS can claim to be their own, it is vegetarian dishes! That is our USP and our biggest draw!!

For some other cultures, veggie is nothing but bald and bland dishes, fillers and also-rans listed lower down in the wedding or banquet menu, rice/noodles. Or 'mock' dishes made with soy to look like meat - even there they can't ignore meat!!

@PMOIndia @DrSJaishankar @MEAIndia or whoever decided to showcase India's varied, diverse and unique vegetarian cuisine have done a great job!!

Yes, they could have offered meat dishes too but that takes the focus away from what we should be proud of. And for the most part it is not ours. We might as well serve pork schnitzel.

text:
🚨 Gov. Gavin Newsom traveled to South Carolina to defend California's Medi-Cal expansion for undocumented immigrants, even as his own administration moved to freeze enrollment and charge new premiums back home.

California launched what officials described as the nation's largest expansion of taxpayer-financed health care for immigrants living in the U.S. illegally, through its Medi-Cal program. The program carried an estimated cost of roughly $2.4 billion annually. State officials also disclosed that California borrowed $3.4 billion to pay health insurers, doctors, and hospitals caring for Medi-Cal patients.

Newsom made the remarks during stops in South Carolina beginning September 3, 2026, as part of his "Take It Back" tour, with about 150 people attending his first appearance in Hardeeville. At those stops, he contrasted California's record with South Carolina's, pointing to South Carolina's $7.25/hour minimum wage and the state's refusal to expand Medicaid under the ACA. The visits come as Newsom, a potential 2028 presidential contender, makes trips to early-voting states ahead of the midterm elections. Back in California, however, Newsom had proposed freezing 2026 adult Medicaid enrollment for undocumented immigrants and requiring those remaining on the program to pay $100 per month starting in 2027, a move projected to save the state more than $5 billion.

What do you think: should states be able to offer government-funded health care to undocumented immigrants, and who should bear the cost? 👇

Where Porsche motorsport heritage meets modern luxury SUV perfection

The Cayenne story began in 2002 — a bold move by Porsche to blend their legendary sports car DNA with practical SUV capability. 

Purists doubted; drivers fell in love. 
By its third generation (launched 2017), and with the stunning Coupé variant arriving in 2019, the Cayenne had evolved into a masterpiece: sharper, sleeker, more athletic — yet every bit the long-distance grand tourer and off-road-capable pioneer.

This 2020 Cayenne Coupé represents the very peak of that early third-generation Coupé design — refined, proven, and built with the uncompromising engineering standards that have kept Porsche at the top for over 75 years. 
Every line, every component, reflects decades of racing innovation transferred to the road.

WHAT MAKES THIS SPECIAL
Let’s break down why this exact specification stands out — not just as an SUV, but as a true Porsche:

⚙️ Powertrain & Performance
3,000cc V6 Petrol Engine: 
The legendary 3.0L V6 is Porsche’s workhorse — smooth, responsive, and brilliantly balanced. 
It delivers effortless power across the rev range, designed for both spirited driving and relaxed cruising.

Tiptronic 4WD: 
Porsche’s renowned 8-speed Tiptronic automatic transmission offers lightning-fast shifts when you want them, seamless refinement when you don’t. 
Paired with permanent all-wheel drive, it delivers confidence on Nairobi’s tarmac, wet roads, or uneven terrain — distributing power intelligently for maximum grip and stability.

✅ SPORTS CHRONO PACKAGE: 
This is NOT just an option — it’s Porsche’s signature performance upgrade. 
It adds a stopwatch on the dash, Sport Plus mode, and engine/transmission tuning that sharpens throttle response, holds gears longer, and adjusts suspension for maximum agility. This is the package that turns a great SUV into a Porsche.

 Comfort, Tech & Engineering
Air Suspension: 
Unlike standard steel springs, Porsche Active Suspension Management (PASM) with air suspension lets you adjust ride height and firmness. Glide like a luxury sedan or raise it for clearance — the best of both worlds.

LED Matrix Headlights + PDLS+: 
Porsche Dynamic Light System Plus automatically adapts your beam pattern, range, and direction based on speed, traffic, and steering angle. Brilliant night visibility without blinding other drivers — pure Porsche intelligence.

Panoramic Glass Roof: 
Floods the cabin with light; reinforces that open, grand-touring feel while keeping you perfectly insulated.

21" Exclusive Wheels: 
Factory-original Cayenne Exclusive design — stronger, lighter, and styled to match the Coupé’s silhouette perfectly.
Porsche Entry & Drive + Power Seats + Heated Seats: Keyless convenience, perfect seating position at the touch of a button, and warmth on cool mornings — thoughtful, enduring luxury.

Navigation + Rear/Parking Camera: 
High-resolution mapping and 360° visibility make navigating Nairobi streets or parking in tight spaces effortless.
